reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.stochasticIntegralBrownianLp -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the Ito integral int_0^t Z dW against the standing Brownian motion as an L^2(P)
class at each time t (sec. 3/4: an L^2 martingale with E|int_0^t Z dW|^2 = E int_0^t |Z|^2).
Faithful Lean: an Lp R 2 P-valued function of t (or of the integrand and t) equal to the L^2
limit of simple integrals up to t, for square-integrable integrands adapted/predictable w.r.t.
the filtration in which the paper's integrands live (augmented joint filtration of W, N, F_0)
with W Brownian for it. Same caveats as stochasticIntegralBrownian: the reference filtration
must not be smaller than the paper's (otherwise the paper's integrands fall into the junk
branch); junk outside the class harmless only under restriction.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.stochasticIntegralBrownianLp (ItoL2CompletionMaster.lean:302-305)

Reading: Lp R 2 P-valued function of t equal to the L^2 limit of simple integrals up to t, for
square-integrable integrands adapted to the paper's filtration with W Brownian for it; junk
outside harmless only under restriction.
Lean: stochasticIntegralBrownianLp t := Filter.limUnder atTop (fun n => masterLp ... t n). For
t >= 0 the sequence is Cauchy (masterLp_cauchySeq) in the complete space Lp R 2 P, so limUnder is
its limit (used in masterApprox_tendsto_L2); for t < 0 the sequence is constantly 0 and the limit
is 0. The limit lies in lpMeas for F t (stochasticIntegralBrownianLp_mem_lpMeas). Filtration F a
parameter with IsBrownianFiltration W F; integrand hypotheses are arguments (no junk). Matches
the reading; the limUnder encoding is a representation choice (it would be junk only for a
non-convergent sequence, which does not occur).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Choices: (1) The limit is taken with Filter.limUnder, which returns the limit whenever the
sequence converges; masterLp t n is Cauchy for t >= 0 in the complete space Lp R 2 P and constant
0 for t < 0, so limUnder is always the genuine L^2 limit (no junk value). (2) The value 0 at
negative times is the integral up to a negative time. (3) Integrand class and filtration as for
stochasticIntegralBrownian (progressive, finite energy on every horizon, F a parameter set to the
paper's filtration by the propositions).
